Are you worried about your landlord increasing rent? The rules differ depending on your state. In this DocOga Deep-Dive, we break down rent increase laws in Enugu and Lagos, showing you your rights and how to protect your finances. Learn about Enugu's unique 15% cap and the process for challenging unreasonable increases in Lagos. Paper beats memory: always get a written agreement and receipts!

sections.title: Lagos: No Cap, But a Remedy

beats.head: Rent Don Increase!
beats.sub: That common phrase that makes every tenant sweat.

beats.head: Budget Sweating?
beats.sub: Unexpected rent hikes can throw your life off balance.

beats.head: You Have Rights!
beats.sub: Don't feel helpless, the law is on your side.

beats.head: States Differ
beats.sub: Enugu and Lagos have different rules for rent increases.

beats.head: Enugu's Hard Cap
beats.sub: A strong protection for tenants against excessive increases.

beats.head: 15% Maximum
beats.sub: Rent increase cannot exceed 15% of existing rent.

beats.head: 2-Year Stability
beats.sub: Review only after second anniversary of your tenancy.

beats.head: Example: ₦400k to ₦460k
beats.sub: ₦400,000 rent can only go to ₦460,000 after 2 years.

beats.head: 3 Conditions Apply
beats.sub: These must all be met for the Enugu cap to work.

beats.head: By Agreement
beats.sub: Landlord and tenant must agree; no unilateral increases.

beats.head: After 2 Years
beats.sub: No increase before the second anniversary of your tenancy.

beats.head: Not Over 15%
beats.sub: The increase must stay within the 15% legal limit.

beats.head: Lagos: No Cap
beats.sub: No statutory percentage cap on rent increases here.

beats.head: Crucial Point
beats.sub: Many tenants misunderstand Lagos's specific rules.

beats.head: S.37 Remedy
beats.sub: You can challenge an unreasonable increase in court.

beats.head: Legal Avenue
beats.sub: You have a legal path, even without a percentage cap.

beats.head: Challenge Procedure
beats.sub: How to dispute rent increase in Lagos courts.

beats.head: Form TL11 Application
beats.sub: Apply to Magistrates’ Court for order against increase.

beats.head: Court Weighs Factors
beats.sub: Locality rent levels, witnesses, special circumstances.

beats.head: Order Specific Amount
beats.sub: Court can change increase to a reasonable figure.

beats.head: No Eviction Pending
beats.sub: Landlord cannot eject you while application is pending.

beats.head: Bills ≠ Law
beats.sub: Proposed laws are not yet legally binding.

beats.head: Federal Motion
beats.sub: House of Reps motion is a resolution, not a law.

beats.head: Lagos Bill Pending
beats.sub: Tenancy Law 2011 is still the law, not the bill.

beats.head: Enugu Bills Too
beats.sub: New bills are still pending, not yet signed into law.

beats.head: Cite Law, Not Bill
beats.sub: Refer to current law, not what is proposed.

beats.head: New Tenants' Rent
beats.sub: Rules differ for new vs. sitting tenants.

beats.head: Sitting Tenants First
beats.sub: Caps and challenges are mainly for existing tenancies.

beats.head: As Agreed
beats.sub: Rent for vacant property is 'as agreed' by parties.

beats.head: Rent-Increase Anger

beats.head: Insist on Receipt

claims.text: In Enugu a rent increase may not exceed 15% of the existing rent, and rent may be reviewed only after every second anniversary of the tenancy.

The section as quoted: “rent chargeable for letting of any accommodation within the State shall be as agreed between the landlord and the tenant, and may be reviewed by the parties after every second anniversary of the tenancy created … PROVIDED that the difference between the new and the existing rent shall not exceed 15% of the existing rent”.
A flat let at ₦400,000 a year from 1 January 2025 cannot be reviewed before 1 January 2027, and the new rent may not exceed ₦460,000 (₦400,000 plus 15%).
The review is by the parties — a unilateral increase is ineffective.
Not before the second anniversary.
Not more than 15% above the existing rent.
Enugu’s cap applies to a sitting tenancy being reviewed; it says nothing about the rent a landlord may ask of a new tenant, which remains “as agreed”.
There is no statutory percentage cap on rent increases in Lagos.
Lagos’s remedy is the s.37 application to have an increase declared unreasonable.
On Form TL11 the tenant applies to the Court for an order declaring an increase unreasonable.
The Court issues a hearing notice on Form TL12 and weighs (a) the general level of rents in the locality or a similar locality, (b) evidence of witnesses, and (c) any special circumstances.
If satisfied, it may order on Form TL13 that the increase be changed to a specific amount.
It is unlawful for a landlord to eject a tenant while that application is pending.
There is no federal percentage cap on rent increases.
On 23 October 2025 the House of Representatives adopted a motion urging that rent increases be kept within 20% of the existing rent — a resolution, not a law: it binds no landlord and no court.
The Lagos State Tenancy and Recovery of Premises Bill, 2025 passed second reading on 10 July 2025 and went to the House Committee on Housing, where it still sat in August 2026.
The Tenancy Law of 2011 remains the law of Lagos until the Assembly passes the bill and the Governor assents.
As reported (clause 33): the s.37 right to ask the court to call an increase unreasonable survives, with no eviction while the application is pending; the bill still sets no rent ceiling.
A bill, not law, as at 3 November 2026. Two bills would amend the Landlord and Tenant Law, Cap. 101.
Until the Governor assents and the law is gazetted, the 2008 amendment (rent review only after every second anniversary, no more than 15%) is the newest Enugu law.
An unlawful increment, and a court will not enforce the increased figure.
Lagos is one of the few states that makes a rent receipt a statutory duty and prescribes what must be on it.
If your landlord tries to increase rent before the second anniversary or by more than 15%, you can point to the law and your agreement.
If they still push an unlawful increment, a court will not enforce that increased figure.
Lagos is one of the few states that makes a rent receipt a statutory duty and prescribes what must be on it.
